parameters.content:
## News digest — the supervisor's plan, made static

This is the hand-built twin of what `packages/agent` compiles on the fly for a `source=scheduler` signal (Langfuse trace `bcd6ebda2eba7db1b3786c4258100d8b`). Same five stages, same models, same prompts — no planner LLM, no replan, no tool choice at runtime.

**fetch** → one MCP session, four `tools/call`: the post window, the chat history (dedup corpus) and the two skill files that make up the system prompt.
**map** → one LLM call per chunk, selecting candidate events. Keeps when unsure.
**reduce** → one LLM call composing the single Russian message.
**deliver** → `send_telegram_message` through MCP, so the outgoing text also lands in the `telegram_messages` log the next run dedups against.
**stamp** → the watermark moves only after a confirmed delivery.

Everything configurable lives in **Config**. `telegramChatId` ships as `0` on purpose — set it before the first run.

nodes.name: Every day at 21:00
nodes.notes: Mirrors scheduled_tasks row #4 (cron '0 21 * * *'). The timezone comes from the workflow settings, not from the expression.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: The only place to edit. telegramChatId MUST be set — it is 0 in git on purpose, so no chat id is committed.

nodes.name: Window + MCP calls
nodes.notes: Reads the watermark, opens the window, and emits the four MCP calls this run needs.

nodes.name: MCP: posts + history + skills
nodes.notes: Four tools/call requests on one MCP session: list_news, get_telegram_chat_history, read_skill ×2.

nodes.name: Chunk posts
nodes.notes: Builds the system prompt from the two skills and splits the window into contiguous chunks by character budget. One item per chunk = the map phase.

parameters.text:
=Map pass over one chunk of a split fetch — do NOT compose a digest. Keep candidate events per the skill's categories; when unsure KEEP (the reduce step filters strictly); drop obvious noise (ads, alerts/drone play-by-play without damage, weather, filler, memes, sport). Merge same-event posts into one entry. Do NOT drop events because input.history already mentions them — dedup is the reduce step's job. Output ONLY a JSON array: [{summary: 1–2 фразы на русском с конкретикой (числа, имена, места), category, source_ids, postedAt}]; empty chunk → []

<posts>
{{ $json.postsJson }}
</posts>

<history>
{{ $json.historyJson }}
</history>

nodes.name: Map: select candidates
nodes.notes: Runs once per chunk item. typeVersion 1.7 + batching.batchSize>1 makes the node fire a whole batch concurrently (Promise.allSettled), which is the map phase parallel again. XML input blocks, same rendering as the agent compose step.

nodes.name: Prepare reduce input
nodes.notes: Collects every map result into one selections array — the fan-in.

nodes.name: Reduce: compose digest
nodes.notes: The one step that writes the user-visible text. Output lands in $json.text.

nodes.name: Digest deliverable?
nodes.notes: One message, Telegram-sized. The skill says drop the lowest-priority items instead of splitting.

nodes.name: MCP: send digest
nodes.notes: send_telegram_message goes through MCP on purpose: it also appends the message to the telegram_messages chat log that the next run's dedup reads. A native Telegram node would deliver but leave the log — and therefore the dedup — blind.

nodes.name: Stamp watermark
nodes.notes: Watermark moves only after a confirmed delivery.

parameters.errorMessage: =Digest not deliverable: {{ ($json.text || '').trim().length }} chars (limit {{ $('Config').first().json.maxTelegramChars }}). Nothing was sent and the watermark was not advanced.

nodes.name: Refuse to send
nodes.notes: Fails the execution, which hands the run to the error workflow.

parameters.content:
### Chunking is ours, not MCP's

The agent asks `list_news` for a fixed `chunks: 3` because its plan DSL can only reference `${bind.chunks.0}` statically. n8n iterates over items, so the chunking lives in **Chunk posts** and follows a character budget instead of a fixed count.

### Parallelism

A canvas branch is not a thread — n8n walks branches one after another, and a node normally processes its items in a loop. So the agent's three-way `parallel` step has **no shape on this canvas**: it is one node, run per item.

Two knobs, often confused: **`maxCharsPerChunk`** (Config) decides how many posts go into one call — the context size; **Batch Size** decides how many of those calls run at once — the rate-limit pressure. A batch item is a whole chunk, never a single post.

The chain node still gets it done concurrently: at `typeVersion 1.7+`, **Batch Size** > 1 fires that many items at once (`Promise.allSettled`). Set to 4 here, so a 3-chunk window is one round trip — the same wall time as the agent's fan-out, expressed as a node setting instead of a plan shape.
